clue.text: Manage to put top on wall

definitions.meaning: to manage is to get by or deal with a difficulty successfully
to finish a wall with a capping course of stone or brick, called coping

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: coping with trouble, and capping a wall with its protective topmost layer.

clue.text: Lifting outerwear, one single undergarment

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the word is raised, read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat worn outside
I is the Roman numeral for one
sole means only, single

explanation.surface: Removing an outer coat reveals just one piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Lifting' turns MAC upwards to give CAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sleeveless top worn under clothing is an item of women's underwear.

clue.text: Not all Turandot's courtiers are game

definitions.meaning: in Puccini's opera Turandot the three ministers are Ping, Pang and Pong, so two of them are named

explanation.walkthrough: Puccini's ministers are Ping, Pang and Pong; leaving out Pang gives the other two, which together name table tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the informal name for table tennis, a bat-and-ball game.

clue.text: Grumpy type has to go over a little ground

parts.note: to cross is to go over, as with a bridge or road
a patch is a small piece of land, as in a vegetable patch

explanation.surface: An irritable person must trudge across a small plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered, irritable person is an old colloquial sense of this word.

clue.text: Lecher adopts ultimately corrupt course

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a roue is a debauched man, a lecher

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word corrupt

explanation.surface: A womaniser takes up a path that ends in corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a way or line taken from one place to another; a synonym.

clue.text: After beer, male's in condition where moving is impossible

indicators.note: in tells you the pieces go inside the word for condition

parts.note: state means condition, as in a state of repair

indicators.note: after puts the male piece behind the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Once a man has had his pint, he finds himself unable to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' sets the male letter behind the beer, and 'in' puts that pair inside the condition. The definition is the chess sense: neither side can make a legal move.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess this is the position in which a player has no legal move, so the game is drawn.

clue.text: Business deal not involving a whole BT office?

definitions.text: Business deal not involving a whole BT office?

parts.words: Business deal not involving a whole BT office?
parts.note: a trade in which an old item counts toward the price, read as a piece of a telephone exchange run by BT

explanation.walkthrough: BT (British Telecom) is the UK's main telephone company; its buildings are telephone exchanges, so part of one is a pun on a trade-in deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A transaction where an old car or item is handed over as partial payment for a new one.

clue.text: State with low interest rate.

parts.note: the phrase reads as finance but means a condition in which one's interest, in the sense of engagement, is low

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests banking; the real sense is a state of being bored, when interest is at a low level.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom, a condition of weariness and lack of interest, is a synonym.

clue.text: Hurry with reassuring report on newborn baby's toes?

definitions.meaning: to hurry is to go quickly

definitions.text: reassuring report on newborn baby's toes?
definitions.meaning: a parent told the baby's toes are all present, read as two words: it possesses all ten

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as two words, a reassurance that a baby's toe count is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: To move or act quickly is a straight synonym for hurrying.

clue.text: Sweet, given lots of money

definitions.meaning: a sweet flavoured with peppermint, a confection
a fortune, as in 'that car cost a ...'

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers a peppermint confection and, colloquially, a very large sum of money.

clue.text: Essays a series of trips to the country

definitions.meaning: William Cobbett's collection of essays from his horseback tours of English farmland, published 1830

definitions.text: a series of trips to the country
definitions.meaning: read literally, excursions on horseback through the countryside

explanation.surface: A book of essays describing a run of countryside outings.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense needs some literary knowledge: William Cobbett, the English radical, wrote up his tours of farming districts as a famous book of essays.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobbett's essay collection has this title, and the phrase also literally describes journeys into the countryside.

clue.text: One trained to analyse piece of paper is revealing error

parts.note: a Freudian is a psychoanalyst trained in Sigmund Freud's method
a slip is a small piece of paper

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst's note reveals a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue thought to expose a hidden wish is a mistake that reveals something.

clue.text: Excellent grain said to be set aside

parts.note: super is a colloquial word for excellent

indicators.note: said signals that the word for grain is to be heard rather than written

parts.note: a seed is a grain, as of corn

explanation.surface: Some top-quality corn is supposedly to be put to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To replace or displace something is to set it aside in favour of another; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Release what bird's-nester took, you'd said

indicators.note: said tells you the phrase is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a bird's-nester raids nests for eggs, so this is 'eggs you'd' spoken together

explanation.surface: Someone is told to let go of the eggs a nest-robbing collector stole.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird's-nesting, collecting wild birds' eggs, was a traditional British boyhood pastime, now illegal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ooze out or give off a liquid or smell is to release it slowly; a verb synonym.

clue.text: In Italian one has a tongue all can understand

definitions.text: In Italian one has a tongue all can understand

parts.words: In Italian one has a tongue all can understand
parts.note: the name for a common trading language is itself an Italian phrase, literally 'Frankish tongue', so Italian supplies the term

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is Italian in origin, from the mixed trading language of Mediterranean ports, and now means any shared language used between speakers of different native tongues.
explanation.definitionFit: A common language adopted between people who do not share a mother tongue is exactly what this term names.

clue.text: Outlaws sport in which upper-class twit takes part

indicators.note: in which tells you the twit goes inside the sport

parts.note: fives is a ball game played with the hand against walls, played at English public schools
U is the standard label for upper-class usage
git is British slang for a fool or twit

explanation.surface: Bandits are playing a game that includes a posh idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: FIVES is a handball game played in a walled court, associated with English public schools; 'takes part' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: People on the run from the law are fugitives, a fair match for outlaws.

clue.text: Man of unimpressive physique offering support to runners?

definitions.meaning: a tall stick for runner beans to climb up

explanation.definitionFit: A tall thin person is likened to the stick that supports climbing beans.

clue.text: Singular person that amuses perfectionist

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a tickler is someone who tickles, amusing others

explanation.surface: An unusual entertainer turns out to be a fussy perfectionist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who insists on the exact details is a stickler, one demanding perfection.

clue.text: Lies pregnant, abandoned about to become this?

definitions.text: Lies pregnant, abandoned about to become this?

indicators.note: abandoned suggests letters cast off into disorder, a cue to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A woman expecting a baby lies alone, deserted, and wonders whether she will raise the child alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging LIES PREGNANT (signalled by 'abandoned') gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes how someone comes to be in that situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother left alone by her partner while expecting would raise the child as a lone parent.

clue.text: Balance a number of small plates

definitions.meaning: the thin overlapping plates covering a fish or reptile

explanation.definitionFit: A weighing machine is a pair of scales, and the protective plates of a fish share the word.

clue.text: Love fair-haired type, slightly short, with good shape

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: slightly short means one letter is dropped from the end

parts.note: a blond is a fair-haired person

explanation.surface: Someone loves a slightly short fair-haired person who is in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly short' drops the last letter of BLOND to leave BLON.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is an example of a shape.

clue.text: Logs here the start of presidential route?

definitions.text: Logs here the start of presidential route?

parts.words: Logs here the start of presidential route?
parts.note: a log-built home is where the American myth of humble birth to the White House begins, as with Lincoln

explanation.walkthrough: 'Log cabin to White House' is a classic American phrase for a self-made president's rise, Abraham Lincoln being the famous example.
explanation.definitionFit: A small simple hut made of logs is the starting point of that presidential journey.

clue.text: Awfully nice, seen on wings of theatre stage, and nice on screen too

indicators.note: seen on means placed after what comes before it in the build
the wings of a theatre are its sides, so the outer letters of the word theatre are used

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

indicators.note: awfully signals the word nice is made into a mess, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone very pleasant appears in the theatre wings and on stage, and comes across well on film too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' scrambles the first 'nice' into ENIC, and 'seen on' places it after the theatre's wings and the stage; the second 'nice' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks attractive and appealing on television is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Dropping hammer in Olympic venue, a French city

indicators.note: dropping means removing the named word from the longer one

parts.note: Lillehammer in Norway hosted the 1994 Winter Olympics
taken as written

explanation.surface: Without the hammer throw at the Games, a French city takes its place.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR inserted a stray colon; the page reads 'Olympic venue'. Lillehammer, the 1994 Winter Olympics host, loses HAMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a major city in northern France, near the Belgian border.

clue.text: Right line I must follow in appealing to get cracking

indicators.note: in tells you the first pieces go inside the word for appealing

parts.note: lovely means attractive or appealing
OK means all right, correct

explanation.surface: A sentence about attractive lines of verse that must come in the correct order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' splits the word for appealing after its second letter to take the three pieces; 'must follow' is padding linking them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are imperatives urging someone to hurry up and get moving at once.

clue.text: Sort of tax cut

definitions.meaning: a per-head levy, as in the UK's unpopular 1990 community charge
to crop or lop the top off, as with horns or tree branches

explanation.walkthrough: The UK's 1990 community charge, a flat tax on each adult, was nicknamed after an old word for a head, which also gives the verb meaning to trim.
explanation.definitionFit: A head tax is named from this word for a head, which also means to cut hair or horns short.

clue.text: Clearly indicated one has to put name to Letters to Editor

parts.note: to sign something is to put your name to it
post means mail, letters delivered

explanation.surface: Someone must sign a letter for the newspaper's letters page.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions marked by roadside pointers are clearly shown, giving this sense of plainly indicated.

clue.text: Clothes get women's attention

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, as in menswear or evening wear, the word means clothing.
